statement: U011 is resolved as degeneracy with a precisely bounded exception. A graded interval-membership score is a relaxation of a binary in-force filter: given correct in-force intervals and a correct query date, the in-force version receives the maximum membership, so the graded score reproduces the filter's ordering and cannot beat it - it can only tie or, if mis-tuned, lose. The soft score can therefore differ only when the filter's inputs are wrong or absent, namely unofficial, missing or conflicting effective dates (which the published hard-filter system itself used, from a private source) or an incorrectly inferred query date. Scope is further reduced because the advantage is only observable on substantively changed versions; for editorial amendments the compared versions are interchangeable. The surviving claim is consequently an equivalence-plus-robustness claim about input uncertainty, not a ranking-superiority claim.
